description: 阅读文学散文,讨论哲学,自如切换语域。掌握英语最细微的差别以及 UK/US/Aus 之间的差异。

topics.description: 小说、随笔与高级文学中的语言

guide.intro: 文学英语层次密集,通常在拉丁词源与日耳曼词源之间精心平衡。C2 阶段,作家的语域选择(Latinate vs Germanic)、句长与隐喻使用都是有意为之的工具。中文读者尤需注意:英语「commence / terminate / perceive」类词带有文言式克制,与中文 之 / 然 / 矣 的书面色彩相当;而 Germanic 短词则近乎白话直叙。

sections.text: 英语表达同一概念常有两条路径:盎格鲁-撒克逊词源(短、具体)与拉丁/法语词源(长、抽象)。文学作者借这一选择切换文本的语调。中文学习者常误以为长词总更得体——其实正相反,刻意的 Germanic 短句往往更具文学张力。
散文中叙述视角(第一人称、第三人称、自由间接引语、第二人称)决定语调与距离。「Free indirect speech」(自由间接引语)是英语的标志:不加引号、不带「he said」即可呈现角色的思想。中文白话文虽也有近似手法,但更倚赖句末助词如 罢了 / 也罢 来透露心理。

rows.source: She wondered if he had ever truly loved her. Probably not.
rows.translation: 她在想他是否真的爱过她。大概没有吧。

rows.source: It was not, he reflected, the worst of all possible worlds.
rows.translation: 他寻思,这并不是所有可能世界中最糟的一个。

rows.translation: 夜深;街道,空寂;城市,昏沉。

sections.text: C2 读者应当意识到:逗号也可以与分号同样具有戏剧性。文学语体中,标点常是节奏本身的一部分,正如中文的「、」与「,」差之毫厘。

lessons.title: 对话:读书会上谈小说
lessons.description: 在读书会上讨论叙述者声音与散文风格。

exercises.prompt: 读书会上谈小说

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So, what struck you about the prose? The narrator slips into free indirect speech without warning — did anyone find that disorienting?

turns.speaker: mara
turns.text: I rather liked it. The boundary between her thoughts and the narration dissolves, and we're suddenly complicit in her self-deception.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请以 C2 文学语域评述叙述者的声音
options: What I found most arresting was how the Latinate register surfaces precisely when she most needs to obscure her own motives.
The Latin words are good when she is hiding what she really wants to do.
Yeah, the fancy words come out when she's lying to herself, which is cool.
turns.answer: What I found most arresting was how the Latinate register surfaces precisely when she most needs to obscure her own motives.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Beautifully put. And the recurring image of the shuttered window — were you reading it as straightforwardly symbolic, or working harder than that?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 文学评论中常见的 hedging 表达
turns.before: It functions less as symbol than as motif,
turns.after: — gathering meaning with each iteration rather than announcing it.
turns.answer: I'd argue

turns.speaker: mara
turns.text: That's exactly the distinction I was groping for. A symbol declares itself; a motif accrues weight.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请优雅地表达不同意见
options: I take the point, though I'd hesitate to draw the line quite so cleanly — the shutter does, at moments, behave symbolically.
No, you are wrong about that, it is clearly a symbol every time.
I take the point, but the shutter is, like, totally a symbol, you know?
turns.answer: I take the point, though I'd hesitate to draw the line quite so cleanly — the shutter does, at moments, behave symbolically.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Lovely tension to leave on. Shall we turn to the ending? Earned, or contrived?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请带一点保留地下文学判断
options: Earned, on balance — though the final paragraph teeters on the edge of sentimentality without quite tipping over.
It is earned, completely and without any question whatsoever.
Contrived, no doubt about it, total cop-out.
turns.answer: Earned, on balance — though the final paragraph teeters on the edge of sentimentality without quite tipping over.

turns.speaker: mara
turns.text: Teeters is generous. I think she falls.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And on that delicious disagreement, let's break for wine.

guide.intro: 修辞依托三大支柱:ethos(品格)、pathos(情感)、logos(逻辑)。C2 演说者会构造能引发听众思考的句子,熟悉古典修辞格。中文写作传统讲究「起承转合」,英语社论则讲究「thesis → argument → refutation → call to action」——两者节奏不同,需要切换。

rows: We shall fight on the beaches; we shall fight on the landing grounds…
Government of the people, by the people, for the people.
Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.
It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
Veni, vidi, vici (I came, I saw, I conquered).

sections.text: Op-ed(社论)英文以论点开篇,用证据支撑,承认并驳斥对方,以呼吁(call to action)收束。句长在短促与绵长之间切换节奏。中文社论常用「不得不说」「值得深思」类钩子,英语则偏好「Make no mistake」「To suggest otherwise is to ignore the evidence」。

rows.source: Make no mistake: this policy will define a generation.
rows.translation: 毋庸讳言:这项政策将定义一整代人。

rows.source: To suggest otherwise is to ignore the evidence.
rows.translation: 若作他论,等同无视证据。

rows.source: We owe it to ourselves — and to those who come after — to act now.
rows.translation: 我们既亏欠自己,也亏欠后来者——必须现在行动。

sections.text: 中文里「我们大家」对应英语 'we, as a society' 或干脆只用 'we'。加上 'as a society' 会让语气更克制、更具公共性。

exercises.explanation: 中文 L1 直译陷阱:「客气一点说」 不是 「speak more politely」(这是「说话再礼貌一点」的命令),而是固定的让步表达式 「to put it mildly / to put it kindly / to put it generously」。C2 写作中是常用 understatement(克制陈述)。

lessons.title: 对话:与编辑修改社论
lessons.description: 在报社与编辑一起打磨你的专栏稿——修辞格与 hedging。

exercises.prompt: 与编辑修改社论

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: The argument's solid, but the lede is doing too much heavy lifting. You're asserting where you should be insinuating. Soften the verbs.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 接受编辑关于 hedging 的建议
options: Fair point — I'll recast 'proves' as 'suggests' and let the reader do the arithmetic.
OK, I will make the words less strong, that is a fair point.
Sure, I'll dial down the rhetoric so it's not so in-your-face, totally.
turns.answer: Fair point — I'll recast 'proves' as 'suggests' and let the reader do the arithmetic.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Better. Now, paragraph three — that tricolon. It's clean, but it lands as glib. Either earn it or cut it.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 一个修辞动词——让一个修辞格物有所值
turns.before: I take your point — let me see whether the tricolon
turns.after: its keep before I sacrifice it.
turns.answer: earns

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Good. And the kicker — you're hedging there in a way that reads as cowardice rather than nuance. Pick a side, or commit to your ambivalence.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 针对编辑的批评,捍卫这种模棱两可
options: I'd push back, gently — the ambivalence isn't a hedge, it's the argument. To resolve it would be to misrepresent the evidence.
I disagree with you, the not-deciding is the actual point of the piece.
Nah, that's me sitting on the fence on purpose, it's literally the whole point.
turns.answer: I'd push back, gently — the ambivalence isn't a hedge, it's the argument. To resolve it would be to misrepresent the evidence.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Fair — though if that's the move, the kicker has to signal it. As written, it reads as flinching.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 用一个修辞格回应——提出 antithesis
options: Then let me rebuild it with an antithesis — 'not certainty, but the courage of uncertainty' — something to that effect.
I will make the ending have two opposite words to make it stronger.
I'll throw in some literary device, you know, like 'A but not A' or whatever.
turns.answer: Then let me rebuild it with an antithesis — 'not certainty, but the courage of uncertainty' — something to that effect.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: And the headline — it's serviceable, but it doesn't earn the piece beneath it. Can you give me something that whispers rather than shouts?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 用于 hedging 的柔和情态动词
turns.before: Let me try — something like 'Why the certainty is the symptom' — that
turns.answer: might

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Now you're cooking. Send me a fresh draft by six and we'll run it tomorrow.

guide.intro: 哲学文本是英语名词化(nominalization)最密集的体裁。「to be / to know」一类基本动词常被转为名词:being, knowing, becoming, awareness。C2 阅读者应能从这种密度中读出论证结构。中文学习者需注意:汉语「之」「者」可以承担轻量名物化,但英语的 -ness / -ity / -ion 名词化往往会让句子结构更长更抽象。

lessons.title: 对话:哲学研讨课上的概念辩论
lessons.description: 在博士研讨课上讨论「自由」概念的界定——情态细微差别密集。

exercises.prompt: 哲学研讨课上的自由概念

turns.speaker: prof
turns.text: Let's begin from a deceptively simple question: when we say an agent could have done otherwise, what is the modal force of that 'could'?

turns.speaker: rina
turns.text: I'd read it as nomological possibility — consistent with the laws of nature, given the actual state of the world.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 用情态细微差别提出反方立场
options: I'd want to distinguish that from a weaker reading on which 'could' tracks merely epistemic possibility — what, for all we know, might have obtained.
I think we should say 'could' just means we don't know what could happen.
Yeah but maybe 'could' just means like, anything could happen, you know?
turns.answer: I'd want to distinguish that from a weaker reading on which 'could' tracks merely epistemic possibility — what, for all we know, might have obtained.

turns.speaker: prof
turns.text: Good. And on the nomological reading, are we already conceding too much to the compatibilist? Rina?

turns.speaker: rina
turns.text: Possibly, yes — though I'd want to hear the counter-move before I commit.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 在哲学辩论中使用一个情态助动词
turns.after: grant the laws-plus-state reading while denying that this exhausts what we mean by 'could'.
turns.answer: could

turns.speaker: prof
turns.text: Now you're making the move I was hoping someone would make. Press on it.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 把论证推进到 C2 水平
options: The thought is that 'could have done otherwise' tracks something agential — a capacity exercised — and capacities aren't reducible to the modal profile of physical states.
The idea is that doing things is about the person, not about science laws and stuff.
Like, 'could have' is about you, not physics, capisce?
turns.answer: The thought is that 'could have done otherwise' tracks something agential — a capacity exercised — and capacities aren't reducible to the modal profile of physical states.

turns.speaker: rina
turns.text: But now you owe us an account of capacity that doesn't smuggle modality back in through the side door.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 用哲学家的口吻作出让步
options: I'll concede that's the genuine difficulty — though I'd resist the suggestion that the regress is vicious rather than merely uncomfortable.
OK that is a problem but maybe it is not a real problem.
Touché — but, like, the loop isn't bad-bad, just awkward-bad.
turns.answer: I'll concede that's the genuine difficulty — though I'd resist the suggestion that the regress is vicious rather than merely uncomfortable.

turns.speaker: prof
turns.text: Excellent. We'll return to whether 'merely uncomfortable' will do, next week.

guide.intro: C2 最难的技能是「读音读语气」。英语——尤其是英式英语——擅长以贬代褒、以褒代贬,以及 litotes(用双重否定表达肯定)。「Not bad」其实是「相当不错」;「I might disagree slightly」常常意味着「我激烈反对」。中文有「反语」,但中文反语多靠语气助词与上下文,英语则可能直接靠 deadpan(冷面)语调,而书面文字里所有线索都得从修辞与上下文中提取。

topics.title: 诗与典故——辨认
topics.description: 十四行诗、自由诗与现代散文中的古典典故

guide.intro: C2 不要求你写诗,但要求你辨认。英语是建立在「重音音节」之上的语言;中文则按字调(平仄)区分。因此 iambic pentameter(te-TUM × 5)对我们而言是「识别层面」的任务。此外,《圣经》和莎士比亚的句子在现代英语散文中作为典故反复出现——中文学习者若不知出处会读漏关键语气。

sections.text: 英语中每个音节都有重音值。「iamb」= 弱 + 强(te-TUM)。「pentameter」= 五个 iamb。「Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?」=「SHALL i com-PARE thee TO a SUM-mer's DAY」。中文以字调为主,音节重音相对均匀——因此这一节我们的目标是「辨认」,不是「创作」。

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: Chapters four through seven. The middle sags because you're protecting the protagonist from the consequences you've already set up. The reader senses the flinching.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 文学自省式动词

turns.speaker: ed

turns.answer: Honestly? No. That scene gave me trouble — I rewrote it eleven times and I think the eleventh draft is where the voice gave up.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: Then let's rebuild it from the first draft. Trust the voice that got you here — the workshop instinct is the enemy.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 以专业方式接受编辑最后的提醒

Cool, I'll bash through it and ping you when it's done.
turns.answer: Understood. Give me three weeks for the structural and another two for the dinner scene — I'd rather come back with something cleaner than rush a half-fix.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: One last thing — the epilogue. Drop it. The novel ends two pages earlier, on the image of the empty platform. The epilogue is you reassuring yourself.

turns.speaker: you

turns.speaker: ed
